ctx.x: Yes, he was married. We were playing with Tommy Dorsey, this was now 1937 and we were playing at a black theatre called the Nixon's Grand Theatre in Philadelphia and in the chorus, it was a black chorus, as you know, and a black pit band, marvelous band and of course, marvelous black dancers, but we were the attraction because Tommy had become a big thing and we sold the theatre out, and there were great comedians like Pigment Markham and he and I became friends and there was a little gin mill that we used to go…

Now, I went to the bandleader of the Sunset Royal Band and I said, 'Would you mind very much if we dated the girls. We're going to be here a week and we'd love to take them out.' And the man said, 'Go ahead,' there was no jealousy, he was so nice about it, and he said, 'Go ahead, it's cool, great, we're glad,' because there wasn't too much of that going on and it hadn't really begun, so we, Dave Tough and I fell madly in love with two lovely girls in the show, and Dave married his lady friend and my lady friend…
